slot.brief: Count the number of ways to select r objects from n distinct types with at least one of a kind excluded, or a committee with simple restrictions; easy case count.

stem: A committee of $3$ is selected from $8$ people, including P and Q. How many committees have at least one of P and Q absent?

verdicts.working: Total committees: \(\binom{8}{3}=56\). Committees containing both P and Q: \(6\). Thus \(56-6=50\).

working:
$\text{Total}=\binom{8}{3}=56$; committees containing both P and Q: $\binom{6}{1}=6$. Required $=56-6=50$.

Independent check: Total committees: \(\binom{8}{3}=56\). Committees containing both P and Q: \(6\). Thus \(56-6=50\).
solution:
A committee fails the condition only if it contains both P and Q. Thus,
$$\binom{8}{3}-\binom{6}{1}=56-6=50.$$
